activity.title: Inferencing
activity.skill: Clue-based textual inference and evidence lookup

sections.title: Part 1: Quick Inferences
sections.passage:
As the building swayed Jackie watched in horror as hundreds of books tumbled on to the floor.

Few palm trees are found beyond the coast.

Cars whizzed past on either side of Abby as she waited to cross to the other side of the road

responses.prompt: Where are you most likely to find palm trees?

sections.title: THE RIDER
sections.passage: Riding bareback at full gallop was frightening for a young. inexperienced rider like me. When we got to the river the horse immediately stopped. I didn't.

sections.title: BOB
sections.passage: Bob trotted along beside Dave. Suddenly there was a bark and a flash of white and Bob was gone, racing across the road. Before Dave fully realised what was happening there was a screech of brakes and a dull thud.

sections.title: THE MAN
sections.passage:
The light shone briefly on him. then moved on, and he was in darkness again. As he walked through the gloom to his front door, the only sound in the still night, other than his footsteps, was the washing of the waves that encircled his world. He was bathed in fight again. By the time he reached the door, he had been illuminated no less than five times.

In the morning, fishing rod in his hand. he climbed down to his favourite place on the rocks, intending to spend an hour or two there. He could see a launch in the distance and he looked up every now and then, following its progress until it disappeared from his view around the point.

Large ships, yachts and launches of all sizes often passed his isolated home, but the rocks meant that attempting a landing could be dangerous. You had to be a special person to live this sort of life, he reflected happily, as he pulled in another fish.

responses.prompt: Did he often go fishing? How do you know that?
responses.response: he does because he went fishing and got a fish

responses.prompt: Does this story suggest he had many visitors? How do you know that?
responses.response: no because he was fishing by himself

responses.prompt: Was he lonely? How do you know that?

questionScores.rationale: 'In the building' is too vague — does not identify a books-related location such as a library or bookshop.
'Beyond the coast' is the opposite of the correct answer — the text says few palm trees are found beyond the coast, meaning they are found near/at the coast.
Correctly infers the rider fell off when the horse stopped suddenly.
'Horse' is rejected — the bark is the key clue that Bob is a dog.
'He spooked' is too soft/incomplete — the screech of brakes and dull thud indicate Bob was hit by a car.
Correctly identifies a location by the sea/coast.
'The sun' is rejected — the scene is explicitly at night ('in darkness again', 'the still night'), so the light is a lighthouse beam.
Correctly cites that he went fishing and caught a fish as evidence of a regular routine.
Correct answer 'no', but the reasoning given (fishing alone) doesn't address the actual textual evidence — that boats pass his isolated home but rarely land there.
Does not answer yes/no, and cites being alone as if it were evidence of loneliness, when the text instead shows he 'reflected happily' about his life — the opposite of lonely.
